Suggested reading: [Volume 1 · Chapters 19, 28](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-1-9780138229634) · [Volume 2 · Chapters 5](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Follow a lease beyond DORA

DORA describes a common initial IPv4 lease. During renewal a client can unicast to its server; rebinding can seek another server. Address, mask, gateway, DNS options and lease state all matter. Link-local assignment warrants investigation rather than assuming a valid routed enterprise lease.

##### Separate names from application access

A resolver may answer from cache until TTL expiry or obtain an answer from other servers. A/AAAA resolution does not prove that an application transport is reachable. PTR reverse lookup is separate from forward name-to-address resolution.

##### Worked review check

A hostname resolves but HTTPS times out. Is changing DNS necessarily the next step?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

No. Verify the returned address, then the route, security filters, transport and server. A name answer alone does not prove application reachability.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Provide a small DHCPv4 scope and device DNS resolution.

**Covered features:** DHCP DORA/options; DNS record roles; Ports; Relay relationship.

##### Provide addresses on a connected router LAN

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** IOS XE router · Catalyst 8000V/8000 lab · feature/license support required

The DNS server address must represent a real reachable resolver in your lab. The pool sends client options; it does not install a DNS server or create A/AAAA records.

```text
enable
configure terminal
interface GigabitEthernet1
 ip address 10.10.10.1 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown
exit
ip dhcp excluded-address 10.10.10.1 10.10.10.20
ip dhcp pool USERS
 network 10.10.10.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 10.10.10.1
 dns-server 192.0.2.53
 domain-name lab.example
end
```


##### Configure DNS for the router’s own lookups

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** IOS XE router · Catalyst 8000V/8000 lab · feature/license support required

This resolver setting belongs to the router itself; clients obtain their DNS setting from the DHCP pool or their local configuration.

```text
enable
configure terminal
ip domain lookup
ip name-server 192.0.2.53
end
```


##### Verify leases and the DNS service path

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** IOS XE router · Catalyst 8000V/8000 lab · feature/license support required

A DHCP binding does not prove DNS works. A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/PTR records are managed on the DNS service, not by a generic IOS switch command.

```text
show ip dhcp pool
show ip dhcp binding
show ip dhcp conflict
show hosts
ping example.com
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- Pool exhaustion, a wrong mask and an incorrect gateway/DNS option produce different symptoms.
- If the server is on another subnet, configure the relay in lesson 4.6.

##### Command references

- [Catalyst 8000V router documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/routers/catalyst-8000v-edge-software/series.html)
- [Catalyst 9300 configuration and command references](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/catalyst-9300-series-switches/series.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
Client DHCP: Discover → Offer → Request → Acknowledge
DNS: www.example.com → A 192.0.2.80
A valid lease can still contain the wrong DNS server or gateway.
```


#### Check your understanding

Which DNS record stores an IPv6 address?

- **A.** A
- **B.** MX
- **C.** AAAA
- **D.** PTR

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**C. AAAA**

AAAA records contain IPv6 addresses; A records contain IPv4 addresses.

</details>

Next objective: [4.4 SNMP in network operations](#objective-4-4)

<a id="objective-4-4"></a>

### 4.4 — SNMP in network operations

**Exam target:** Explain.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/4.4) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/4.4/commands)

SNMP lets management stations read and sometimes change device information organized in a MIB.

#### Build your understanding

- An SNMP manager queries an agent on a network device. OIDs identify managed objects such as interface counters. Polling obtains values; traps and informs send event notifications.
- Agents commonly listen on UDP 161; notifications commonly use UDP 162. Traps are unacknowledged; informs request acknowledgment.
- SNMPv1/v2c use community strings without modern transport protection. SNMPv3 can provide authentication and privacy (authPriv); authorize only the required views and restrict management sources.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 2 · Chapters 17](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Compare polling and notifications

Get/GetNext/GetBulk retrieve managed values; Set changes writable objects. OIDs identify objects in the MIB. Traps lack acknowledgments while informs request them. Notifications complement polling rather than automatically forming a complete counter history.

##### Apply the actual protection level

SNMPv3 noAuthNoPriv, authNoPriv and authPriv provide different protection. Authentication does not imply encryption. Restrict manager sources, permitted views and write capability. Community-based v1/v2c is useful to recognize in older material; current secure designs need appropriate v3 protection.

##### Worked review check

Does authNoPriv hide monitored counters from traffic observers?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

No. It authenticates messages but does not supply payload privacy. Properly configured authPriv adds encryption.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Configure authenticated and encrypted SNMPv3 polling.

**Covered features:** Manager/agent/MIB; Polling/traps/informs; SNMPv3 authPriv.

##### Restrict the manager and create an authPriv user

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

Replace both secrets and configure matching settings on the NMS. The read-only view covers the MIB in this learning example; narrow it for the intended monitoring task. SHA-2 support must be present on the selected image.

```text
enable
configure terminal
ip access-list standard SNMP-MANAGERS
 permit host 192.0.2.50
exit
snmp-server view STUDY iso included
snmp-server group NMS v3 priv read STUDY access SNMP-MANAGERS
snmp-server user monitor NMS v3 auth sha-2 256 <AUTH_SECRET> priv aes 128 <PRIVACY_SECRET>
end
```


##### Inspect group, user and agent counters

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

SNMP users may not appear as plaintext entries in show running-config; inspect show snmp user. The management station initiates polling to UDP 161.

```text
show snmp user
show snmp group
show snmp
show ip access-lists SNMP-MANAGERS
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- A user with authNoPriv is not equivalent to the group’s required authPriv level.
- Configure notifications separately if required; traps use UDP 162 and informs request acknowledgments. SNMPv1/v2c community examples are legacy on current XE.

##### Command references

- [Cisco IOS SNMP command reference](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/ios-xml/ios/snmp/command/nm-snmp-cr-book/nm-snmp-cr-s5.html)
- [Cisco C9000 IOS XE resilient infrastructure playbook](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/networking/switches/catalyst-9000-switches/c9000-ios-xe-resilient-infra-pb.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
Monitor: interface octets, errors, CPU and memory.
SNMPv3 levels: noAuthNoPriv → authNoPriv → authPriv
Choose authPriv when authentication and encryption are required.
```


#### Check your understanding

Which SNMPv3 level includes authentication and encryption?

- **A.** public
- **B.** noAuthNoPriv
- **C.** authNoPriv
- **D.** authPriv

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**D. authPriv**

authPriv authenticates messages and encrypts their payload.

</details>

Next objective: [4.5 Syslog facilities and severity](#objective-4-5)

<a id="objective-4-5"></a>

### 4.5 — Syslog facilities and severity

**Exam target:** Describe.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/4.5) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/4.5/commands)

Syslog centralizes event messages so operators can correlate activity across devices.

#### Build your understanding

- Severity runs from 0 (emergency) through 7 (debugging): emergency, alert, critical, error, warning, notification, informational, debugging. Lower numbers indicate more serious conditions.
- A logging threshold includes that level and all numerically lower levels. A trap level of warnings (4) sends severities 0–4, not 5–7.
- Facilities categorize message sources. Use timestamps and synchronized clocks. Traditional syslog often uses UDP 514; transport and security options depend on the platform.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 2 · Chapters 13](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Read the message and destination

Cisco messages commonly use %FACILITY-SEVERITY-MNEMONIC. Console, buffered, remote and terminal-monitor logging are distinct destinations. A message facility/mnemonic and a remote syslog facility setting are not the numeric severity.

##### Apply numerical thresholds

Levels are 0 emergency, 1 alert, 2 critical, 3 error, 4 warning, 5 notification, 6 informational and 7 debugging. A threshold includes its number and lower numbers. Debugging can be expensive; scope it narrowly and stop after collecting the required evidence.

##### Worked review check

Which severities does logging trap notifications send?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

0 through 5 inclusive. Informational 6 and debugging 7 are excluded; other logging destinations can have separate thresholds.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Send timestamped syslog at a chosen severity threshold.

**Covered features:** Facilities; Severity 0–7; Threshold; Buffered/remote logging.

##### Configure buffered and remote lab logging

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

The remote threshold sends severity 0–4; local buffered informational includes 0–6. Plain UDP syslog is unencrypted in this closed-lab example. Use the platform’s supported authenticated TLS logging design for production.

```text
enable
configure terminal
service timestamps log datetime msec
logging buffered 32768 informational
logging host 192.0.2.50
logging trap warnings
logging facility local7
end
```


##### Inspect timestamps, destinations and messages

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

Check destination reachability and collector filters. A threshold of warnings excludes notifications/informational/debugging messages.

```text
show logging
show clock detail
show running-config | include logging|service timestamps
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- Synchronize time before comparing events from multiple devices.
- A facility is a category, not a severity level.

##### Command references

- [Catalyst 9300 configuration and command references](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/catalyst-9300-series-switches/series.html)
- [Cisco C9000 IOS XE resilient infrastructure playbook](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/networking/switches/catalyst-9000-switches/c9000-ios-xe-resilient-infra-pb.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
service timestamps log datetime msec
logging host 192.0.2.50
logging trap warnings
show logging
! Sent: emergency, alert, critical, error, warning
```


#### Check your understanding

With logging trap warnings, which severity is included?

- **A.** Debugging (7)
- **B.** Informational (6)
- **C.** Notification (5)
- **D.** Error (3)

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**D. Error (3)**

The warning threshold is 4 and includes all more severe messages numbered 0 through 4.

</details>

Next objective: [4.6 DHCP clients and relays](#objective-4-6)

<a id="objective-4-6"></a>

### 4.6 — DHCP clients and relays

**Exam target:** Configure and verify.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/4.6) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/4.6/commands)

Routers can obtain an address through DHCP and relay requests for clients on other subnets.

#### Build your understanding

- A router interface can use ip address dhcp as a DHCP client. For downstream hosts, ip helper-address belongs on the interface receiving their broadcasts.
- The relay sets gateway information (giaddr) so the DHCP server can choose the correct subnet pool. The server needs a return route and a correctly scoped pool.
- Check VLAN, relay interface, helper address, pool exhaustion, exclusions, and reachability. IOS helper behavior may also forward other UDP services; restrict according to policy.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 1 · Chapters 6, 19](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-1-9780138229634)

##### Trace a relayed request

A client broadcasts locally. A relay on the client-facing routed interface forwards to the server and supplies gateway information so the server selects a pool. The server needs a usable return path and a correctly scoped pool.

##### Keep client, relay and server distinct

ip address dhcp makes an interface a DHCP client; ip helper-address supplies relay behavior. Neither automatically configures a DHCP server. A Layer 2 switch management client may still need an appropriate default gateway for remote reachability.

##### Worked review check

Does a VLAN 20 access port normally receive the helper-address command?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

No. Configure the relay on VLAN 20’s Layer 3 gateway interface or SVI, which receives the client broadcasts and identifies the client subnet.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Configure a DHCP client and relay broadcasts to a remote server.

**Covered features:** IOS DHCP client; DHCP relay; giaddr; Verification.

##### Get the WAN address from DHCP

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** IOS XE router · Catalyst 8000V/8000 lab · feature/license support required

Use this on an interface connected to a lab DHCP server. It is an alternative to the static outside-address example in lesson 4.1.

```text
enable
configure terminal
interface GigabitEthernet2
 ip address dhcp
 no shutdown
end
```


##### Relay a client subnet to a remote server

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** IOS XE router · Catalyst 8000V/8000 lab · feature/license support required

Place the helper on the client-facing Layer 3 interface. The remote server needs a pool for 10.20.20.0/24 and return reachability to the relay. No helper is needed if the server directly shares the client VLAN.

```text
enable
configure terminal
interface GigabitEthernet1
 ip address 10.20.20.1 255.255.255.0
 ip helper-address 192.0.2.10
 no shutdown
end
```


##### Verify client interface, relay and routes

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** IOS XE router · Catalyst 8000V/8000 lab · feature/license support required

Local show ip dhcp binding reports leases served by this IOS device, not every lease on a remote DHCP server. Check the remote server as well.

```text
show dhcp lease
show ip interface brief
show running-config interface GigabitEthernet1
show ip route 192.0.2.10
ping 192.0.2.10
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- Check the client VLAN and DHCP snooping trust before changing the helper address.
- ip helper-address can forward additional UDP services depending on platform defaults; review the intended forwarding policy.

##### Command references

- [Catalyst 8000V router documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/routers/catalyst-8000v-edge-software/series.html)
- [Catalyst 9300 configuration and command references](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/catalyst-9300-series-switches/series.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
interface g0/0
 ip address dhcp
interface g0/1
 ip address 10.20.0.1 255.255.255.0
 ip helper-address 192.0.2.10
! Client VLAN 20 requests are relayed to 192.0.2.10.
```


#### Check your understanding

Where is ip helper-address configured for a client subnet?

- **A.** The client-facing Layer 3 interface
- **B.** Every access port
- **C.** Only the DNS server
- **D.** The console line

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**A. The client-facing Layer 3 interface**

Configure relay on the routed interface that receives the client’s DHCP broadcasts.

</details>

Next objective: [4.7 QoS per-hop forwarding behavior](#objective-4-7)

<a id="objective-4-7"></a>

### 4.7 — QoS per-hop forwarding behavior

**Exam target:** Explain.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/4.7) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/4.7/commands)

QoS manages contention. It cannot create bandwidth, but it can prioritize delay-sensitive traffic and control congestion.

#### Build your understanding

- Classification identifies traffic; marking labels it, commonly using IP DSCP or Layer 2 CoS. Trust markings only at an intentional boundary.
- Queuing schedules packets during congestion. Low-latency priority queuing supports voice, but must be bounded to prevent starving other traffic. Congestion avoidance can drop selected traffic before a queue is full.
- Policing enforces a rate by dropping or remarking excess traffic. Shaping buffers traffic to smooth bursts toward a configured rate, adding delay. Per-hop behavior describes how each router treats a marked class.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 2 · Chapters 15](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Keep markings distinct

DSCP is a six-bit IP marking; CoS/PCP is three bits in an 802.1Q tag. EF commonly uses DSCP 46, with AF/class-selector values for other behaviors. CoS 5 is not the same encoded field as DSCP 46, although a policy can map them.

##### Understand congestion behavior

Delay is transit time, jitter is delay variation, and loss is missing traffic. Bounded priority scheduling manages contention. Policing drops/remarks excess traffic; shaping buffers it for later transmission. Congestion avoidance can drop selectively before queues fill to influence responsive flows.

##### Worked review check

Why can shaping meet a WAN rate while increasing voice delay?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

Excess packets wait in a queue. The shaping rate, burst interval, queue design and priority policy must balance conformance with latency.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Classify, mark, queue, police and shape on a supported router.

**Covered features:** Classification/marking; Queuing; Congestion avoidance; Policing; Shaping.

##### Classify and mark a lab application

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** IOS XE router · Catalyst 8000V/8000 lab · feature/license support required

The UDP range is a lab classification example, not a universal detector of voice. Mark only trusted/verified traffic and apply supported policies to appropriate interfaces.

```text
enable
configure terminal
ip access-list extended VOICE-SOURCES
 permit udp 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255 any range 16384 32767
exit
class-map match-any LAB-VOICE
 match access-group name VOICE-SOURCES
exit
policy-map MARK-LAB
 class LAB-VOICE
  set dscp ef
exit
exit
interface GigabitEthernet1
 service-policy input MARK-LAB
end
```


##### Demonstrate an egress priority queue

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** IOS XE router · Catalyst 8000V/8000 lab · feature/license support required

This illustrates software-router MQC. Catalyst ASIC QoS has platform-specific queues and restrictions; do not assume the same policy is supported on a switch.

```text
enable
configure terminal
class-map match-any EF-TRAFFIC
 match dscp ef
exit
policy-map WAN-QUEUE
 class EF-TRAFFIC
  priority percent 10
 class class-default
  fair-queue
exit
interface GigabitEthernet2
 service-policy output WAN-QUEUE
end
```


##### Alternative rate controls — inspect syntax first

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** IOS XE router · Catalyst 8000V/8000 lab · feature/license support required

The shaping policy definition alone does not attach it. Apply an alternative policy deliberately; only one policy of the relevant type/direction is supported on many interfaces. Policing uses police rather than shape and drops/remarks excess instead of buffering.

```text
configure terminal
policy-map LAB-SHAPE
 class class-default
  shape average 10000000
end
! Inspect applied policy counters:
show policy-map interface GigabitEthernet2
```


##### Define alternative policing and congestion avoidance policies

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** IOS XE router · Catalyst 8000V/8000 lab · feature/license support required

These are separate policy definitions. Policing enforces a 10 Mbps rate by dropping excess traffic; WRED makes early-drop decisions using DSCP thresholds where supported. Definition alone does not apply a policy: attach the chosen policy in a supported direction instead of a conflicting existing policy. Hardware support, queue model and policy compatibility must be checked first.

```text
enable
configure terminal
policy-map LAB-POLICE
 class class-default
  police cir 10000000 conform-action transmit exceed-action drop
exit
exit
policy-map LAB-WRED
 class class-default
  random-detect dscp-based
end
```


##### Verify live classification and queue counters

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** IOS XE router · Catalyst 8000V/8000 lab · feature/license support required

Generate traffic and read matched packets, marks, offered rates and drops. Congestion behavior is meaningful only under load.

```text
show class-map
show policy-map
show policy-map interface GigabitEthernet1
show policy-map interface GigabitEthernet2
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- Bandwidth units, hierarchical support, WRED support and policer syntax vary by forwarding platform.
- Use interface policy counters rather than assuming that a policy definition is active.

##### Command references

- [Catalyst 8000V router documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/routers/catalyst-8000v-edge-software/series.html)
- [Catalyst 9300 configuration and command references](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/catalyst-9300-series-switches/series.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
Pipeline: classify → mark → queue/schedule → transmit
Police: excess packet → drop or remark
Shape:  excess packet → buffer and send later
```


#### Check your understanding

Which mechanism buffers traffic to smooth it to a configured rate?

- **A.** Policing
- **B.** Shaping
- **C.** ARP
- **D.** NAT

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**B. Shaping**

Shaping queues excess traffic for later transmission, while policing generally drops or remarks it.

</details>

Next objective: [4.8 SSH remote access](#objective-4-8)

<a id="objective-4-8"></a>

### 4.8 — SSH remote access

**Exam target:** Configure.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/4.8) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/4.8/commands)

A secure remote CLI requires reachable management addressing, server keys, user authentication and VTY policy.

#### Build your understanding

- Configure a hostname and domain name, generate an RSA key pair, and enable SSH version 2 where supported. The exact key algorithm options vary by IOS version.
- Create a local user with a secret or configure AAA. VTY lines need login local (or an AAA method) and transport input ssh to accept SSH.
- Use access controls to limit management sources. Verify show ip ssh and test the intended user path; console recovery is useful before changing live remote authentication.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 1 · Chapters 6](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-1-9780138229634) · [Volume 2 · Chapters 10](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Verify the access chain

SSH needs operational management addressing, routes, server keys, supported protocol settings, authentication and VTY policy. A password or key alone does not establish a reachable encrypted service. Configure the intended VTY range for the specific platform.

##### Distinguish control locations

A VTY access-class restricts login sources; ip access-group on an interface filters packets through that interface. These are different policy locations. Verify allowed sources and recovery access before changing remote authentication or filtering.

##### Worked review check

Old management clients use SSH successfully but a new subnet cannot. What should be inspected?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

The VTY access-class source matches, routing and any interface ACLs. Regenerating working server keys is not the first response to a source-specific policy problem.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Build, restrict and verify an SSH management path.

**Covered features:** Hostname/domain/key; Local authentication; VTY transport; Management ACL.

##### Configure a secure SSH server

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

A reachable management IP, supported key and user authentication are prerequisites. Start from the console; do not regenerate a key already used for active sessions without planning the effect.

```text
enable
configure terminal
hostname SW1
ip domain name lab.example
username learner privilege 15 algorithm-type scrypt secret <UNIQUE_LAB_SECRET>
crypto key generate rsa general-keys modulus 3072
ip ssh version 2
ip ssh time-out 60
ip ssh authentication-retries 3
line vty 0 15
 login local
 transport input ssh
 exec-timeout 10 0
end
```


##### Allow only a designated management subnet

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

Use an actual management subnet and test through it before relying on this filter. An implicit deny rejects sources not explicitly allowed.

```text
enable
configure terminal
ip access-list standard VTY-MANAGEMENT
 permit 10.99.99.0 0.0.0.255
exit
line vty 0 15
 access-class VTY-MANAGEMENT in
end
```


##### Verify and connect

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x; final command is an IOS SSH client

The client command needs a reachable target with SSH configured. On a workstation, use ssh learner@10.99.99.2 instead.

```text
show ip ssh
show ssh
show users
show access-lists VTY-MANAGEMENT
ssh -l learner 10.99.99.2
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- A valid login from the wrong source network is still denied by the VTY access-class.
- Confirm VTY ranges and secure algorithms supported by the actual release.

##### Command references

- [Cisco C9000 IOS XE resilient infrastructure playbook](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/networking/switches/catalyst-9000-switches/c9000-ios-xe-resilient-infra-pb.html)
- [Catalyst 9300 configuration and command references](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/catalyst-9300-series-switches/series.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
hostname R1
ip domain-name lab.example
crypto key generate rsa modulus 2048
ip ssh version 2
username learner privilege 15 secret LabPassword123
line vty 0 4
 login local
 transport input ssh
```


#### Check your understanding

Which VTY command restricts incoming sessions to SSH?

- **A.** login
- **B.** transport input ssh
- **C.** service password-encryption
- **D.** ip routing

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**B. transport input ssh**

transport input ssh permits SSH on the VTY lines and excludes Telnet from that configured transport list.

</details>

Next objective: [4.9 TFTP and FTP capabilities](#objective-4-9)

<a id="objective-4-9"></a>

### 4.9 — TFTP and FTP capabilities

**Exam target:** Describe.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/4.9) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/4.9/commands)

Network devices use file transfers for software images, configuration backups and recovery.

#### Build your understanding

- TFTP uses UDP 69 for the initial request and dynamically chosen UDP ports for the transfer. It is simple and has no built-in user authentication or encryption.
- FTP uses TCP 21 for control. Active and passive modes establish data channels differently; a firewall must account for the chosen mode. Standard FTP is not encrypted.
- Use secure alternatives such as SCP or SFTP when available and required. Validate image compatibility and integrity, available storage and boot settings before an upgrade.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 2 · Chapters 17](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Know both transfer channels

FTP has a TCP control connection and a separate data connection. Active data commonly originates from server TCP 20; passive data uses a server-advertised port. TFTP starts at UDP 69 then uses negotiated transfer ports. These legacy protocols do not provide confidentiality.

##### Separate copying from upgrading

Verify platform/image compatibility, available storage, vendor-published integrity value, boot settings and installation procedure. Successful copying does not prove an image is appropriate or will boot. Prefer supported secure transfer methods for current deployments.

##### Worked review check

Why is allowing TCP 21 alone sometimes insufficient for FTP?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

It allows control, while the selected active/passive mode also needs a suitable data connection and compatible firewall/NAT handling.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Recognize legacy transfer protocols and use a current secure transfer.

**Covered features:** TFTP; FTP active/passive; SCP alternative; File verification.

##### Copy a configuration using SCP

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x or IOS XE router · Catalyst 8000V/8000 lab · feature/license support required

Use a reachable SSH/SCP server and verify its host identity. The local flash filesystem name may be bootflash: on a router. Protect backup configurations because they contain sensitive operational information.

```text
copy running-config scp:
! Respond to prompts with the lab SCP server and username.
! Keep the password in the interactive password prompt.
dir flash:
show version
```


##### Recognize legacy exam syntax — do not enable it on current XE

**Category:** reference. **Platform/context:** Legacy IOS exam recognition; may be rejected on IOS XE 26.x

TFTP/FTP are unencrypted. Current C9000 resilient infrastructure restrictions can reject these commands. The site does not recommend enabling insecure mode just to run an old example.

```text
! Legacy examples for recognition only:
! copy running-config tftp:
! copy tftp: flash:
! copy running-config ftp:
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- A file transfer is not a complete software upgrade. Validate platform image, hash, boot mode and release-specific upgrade steps separately.
- SCP and SFTP are different protocols; use a transfer mechanism supported by both device and server.

##### Command references

- [Cisco C9000 IOS XE resilient infrastructure playbook](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/networking/switches/catalyst-9000-switches/c9000-ios-xe-resilient-infra-pb.html)
- [Catalyst 8000V router documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/routers/catalyst-8000v-edge-software/series.html)
- [Catalyst 9300 configuration and command references](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/catalyst-9300-series-switches/series.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
copy running-config tftp:
copy tftp: flash:
! Verify image integrity and compatibility before changing boot settings.
! SCP is a different protocol from SFTP.
```


#### Check your understanding

Which statement about TFTP is correct?

- **A.** It encrypts all data
- **B.** It uses TCP 22
- **C.** It has no built-in authentication
- **D.** It requires an FTP account

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**C. It has no built-in authentication**

TFTP is a simple UDP-based transfer protocol without native authentication or encryption.

</details>

Next objective: [5.1 Security threats, weaknesses and mitigation](#objective-5-1)

<a id="domain-5-0"></a>

## 5.0 Security Fundamentals — 15%

Protect devices, traffic, and wireless networks with practical controls.

10 objectives · 0 lettered subtopics

<a id="objective-5-1"></a>

### 5.1 — Security threats, weaknesses and mitigation

**Exam target:** Define.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.1) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.1/commands)

A threat can exploit a vulnerability to cause harm. Risk depends on likelihood and impact, and controls reduce it.

#### Build your understanding

- An exploit is a method of taking advantage of a weakness. Attack vectors include phishing, credential theft, vulnerable software and exposed management services.
- Confidentiality protects data from unauthorized access; integrity protects against unauthorized change; availability keeps services accessible. Controls may be preventive, detective or corrective.
- Mitigation includes patching, segmentation, least privilege, secure configuration and monitoring. No single control eliminates every risk; defense in depth limits the damage from one failure.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 2 · Chapters 9, 10](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Classify the event

Spoofing changes apparent identity, reconnaissance gathers information, denial of service targets availability and a man-in-the-middle can observe or alter traffic. Threat, vulnerability, exploit and business impact describe different parts of risk.

##### Place controls deliberately

Preventive controls reduce likelihood, detective controls identify events and corrective controls limit/repair damage. Patching, segmentation, identity controls, backups and monitoring address different failures. An inline IPS can prevent matching traffic; detection alone does not imply blocking.

##### Worked review check

Does an alert about failed logins establish that guessing was prevented?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

No. The alert is detective evidence. Check separate preventive controls, authentication outcomes and any successful sessions.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Use current platform diagnostics to inspect security exposure.

**Covered features:** Threat/vulnerability/exploit; Risk; Preventive/detective controls.

##### Inventory software and insecure configuration

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

Compare software and hardware to Cisco security advisories and the model’s supported release information. An insecure-configuration report is useful evidence, not a complete vulnerability scan.

```text
show version
show inventory
show system insecure configuration
show ip ssh
show ip http server status
show logging
```


##### Remove plaintext WebUI transport when HTTPS is used

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

Use the configured certificate and management authorization. Disabling a service is one control within a broader threat/risk assessment, not proof that every attack vector is removed.

```text
enable
configure terminal
no ip http server
ip http secure-server
end
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- The current newest release is not automatically the recommended maintenance build for every device.
- Threat modeling, vulnerability assessment and risk acceptance are processes; they are not enabled by a single IOS command.

##### Command references

- [Cisco C9000 IOS XE resilient infrastructure playbook](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/networking/switches/catalyst-9000-switches/c9000-ios-xe-resilient-infra-pb.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
Weak password (vulnerability) + credential guessing (threat activity)
→ unauthorized access (impact)
Controls: MFA, strong secrets, rate limiting, monitoring.
```


#### Check your understanding

An unpatched software flaw is best described as what?

- **A.** A vulnerability
- **B.** An accounting record
- **C.** A guarantee of exploitation
- **D.** An availability control

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**A. A vulnerability**

A vulnerability is a weakness that a threat actor could exploit.

</details>

Next objective: [5.2 Security awareness and physical controls](#objective-5-2)

<a id="objective-5-2"></a>

### 5.2 — Security awareness and physical controls

**Exam target:** Describe.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.2) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.2/commands)

People, processes and physical safeguards are part of network security, not separate from it.

#### Build your understanding

- Train users to recognize phishing, verify unusual requests through a trusted channel, and report incidents promptly. Avoid disclosing credentials or approving unexpected MFA prompts.
- Use locked racks, access badges, visitor procedures, cameras and environmental controls to protect network equipment. Tailgating bypasses physical identity checks.
- Apply documented password and access policies, acceptable-use guidance, onboarding/offboarding and incident response. Physical access to a console or reset button can undermine network controls.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 2 · Chapters 9](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Make policy operational

Awareness, onboarding, offboarding, least privilege and reporting must agree with actual account lifecycle actions. A policy document alone does not revoke an ex-employee’s sessions. Users need a trusted way to report incidents without exposing credentials.

##### Protect physical dependencies

Control access to racks, closets, consoles, removable media and power. Badges, visitor checks and anti-tailgating complement locks. Environmental and power failures can affect availability without a malicious actor.

##### Worked review check

What should offboarding include besides collecting a door badge?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

Revoke or expire relevant logical accounts, VPN access, keys and sessions; review shared credential ownership and the associated records.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Support physical and awareness controls with device evidence.

**Covered features:** Awareness/social engineering; Physical access; Access procedures.

##### Review console/remote users and inventory

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

Use these to support an access review and asset inventory. Locked racks, badges, phishing training and incident reporting are physical/organizational controls outside the Cisco CLI.

```text
show users
show line
show inventory
show logging
```


##### Set an authorized-use banner and console idle timeout

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

A banner communicates an access policy but does not authenticate users or prevent tailgating. Configure console authentication as in lesson 5.3.

```text
enable
configure terminal
banner motd #Authorized lab access only.#
line console 0
 exec-timeout 5 0
end
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- A console session is a privileged physical access path; protect the equipment and recovery procedures.
- Do not mistake a configured banner for a technical access control.

##### Command references

- [Catalyst 9300 configuration and command references](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/catalyst-9300-series-switches/series.html)
- [Cisco C9000 IOS XE resilient infrastructure playbook](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/networking/switches/catalyst-9000-switches/c9000-ios-xe-resilient-infra-pb.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
Suspicious password-reset call → stop → verify using an official contact → report.
Lost badge → revoke access promptly and review activity.
```


#### Check your understanding

Which behavior best addresses a suspicious request for credentials?

- **A.** Reply with the password
- **B.** Verify through a trusted independent channel
- **C.** Disable all logging
- **D.** Share a coworker’s account

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**B. Verify through a trusted independent channel**

Independent verification and reporting reduce the chance of social-engineering success.

</details>

Next objective: [5.3 Local-password device access](#objective-5-3)

<a id="objective-5-3"></a>

### 5.3 — Local-password device access

**Exam target:** Configure and verify.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.3) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.3/commands)

Device access requires controls for console, remote lines and privileged configuration mode.

#### Build your understanding

- Use enable secret for privileged access rather than a legacy enable password. Use username ... secret and login local for local-user authentication.
- Configure console and VTY authentication, timeouts and authorized transports. A line password needs login to activate that line’s password authentication; login local uses the user database instead.
- service password-encryption obscures certain stored plaintext passwords with reversible legacy encoding; it is not strong protection. Use supported strong secret hashes and restrict configuration-file access.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 1 · Chapters 4, 6](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-1-9780138229634) · [Volume 2 · Chapters 10](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Distinguish storage formats

One-way hashes permit secret verification without plaintext storage. Type 7 is reversible legacy obfuscation. Type 8/9 are stronger supported secret hashes; type 6 is reversible AES encryption for recoverable credentials. Storage protection does not encrypt a Telnet session.

##### Read version context

Recognize older line-password and service password-encryption examples for exam interpretation. Current IOS XE defaults and permitted syntax vary by release. Use supported strong secrets and platform-labeled guides; a textbook-era configuration is not a universal current-image template.

##### Worked review check

Does changing an enable password to a strong secret make Telnet confidential?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

No. Credential storage and the management transport are separate. Use an appropriate encrypted transport such as SSH for the session.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Secure privileged mode, local users and access lines.

**Covered features:** Enable secret; User secrets; Console/VTY; Legacy password encoding.

##### Use scrypt-hashed secrets and authenticated access

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

Replace placeholders. SSH key setup is in lesson 4.8. This is the non-AAA local-login path; if AAA is already configured, select an appropriate AAA method list instead of blindly replacing it.

```text
enable
configure terminal
enable algorithm-type scrypt secret <UNIQUE_ENABLE_SECRET>
username learner privilege 15 algorithm-type scrypt secret <UNIQUE_USER_SECRET>
line console 0
 login local
 exec-timeout 5 0
exit
line vty 0 15
 login local
 transport input ssh
 exec-timeout 10 0
end
```


##### Inspect access policy without sharing the secret hashes

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

A hash in configuration is still sensitive. Avoid sharing full running configurations or secret hashes in troubleshooting tickets.

```text
show running-config | section line con
show running-config | section line vty
show ip ssh
show users
show system insecure configuration
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- service password-encryption is legacy reversible obfuscation for some passwords, not an alternative to a strong secret hash.
- Current XE trains may reject weak/legacy secret forms; do not disable hardening to copy an old lab.

##### Command references

- [Cisco C9000 IOS XE resilient infrastructure playbook](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/networking/switches/catalyst-9000-switches/c9000-ios-xe-resilient-infra-pb.html)
- [Catalyst 9300 configuration and command references](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/catalyst-9300-series-switches/series.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
enable secret StrongEnableSecret
username admin secret StrongUserSecret
line console 0
 login local
 exec-timeout 5 0
line vty 0 4
 login local
 transport input ssh
```


#### Check your understanding

Which statement about service password-encryption is correct?

- **A.** It encrypts SSH packets
- **B.** It is a substitute for strong secrets
- **C.** It provides reversible obfuscation for certain passwords
- **D.** It enables MFA

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**C. It provides reversible obfuscation for certain passwords**

The legacy feature obscures some stored passwords and should not be treated as strong cryptographic protection.

</details>

Next objective: [5.4 Password policies and authentication alternatives](#objective-5-4)

<a id="objective-5-4"></a>

### 5.4 — Password policies and authentication alternatives

**Exam target:** Describe.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.4) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.4/commands)

A strong authentication policy balances resistance to guessing, reuse, theft and recovery abuse.

#### Build your understanding

- Use long unique secrets, password managers, controlled recovery and protections against repeated guessing. Avoid shared accounts so activity remains attributable.
- MFA combines different factor categories: something you know, have, or are. Two passwords are both knowledge factors and do not constitute two factor categories.
- Certificates use cryptographic keys and a trust chain to establish identity. Biometrics and security tokens can reduce dependence on passwords but still need enrollment, revocation and recovery policies.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 2 · Chapters 9, 10](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Identify independent proof

Knowledge, possession and inherence describe what is proven, not the number of prompts. Password plus PIN remains two knowledge secrets. A certificate-backed key can prove private-key possession; displaying a public certificate alone cannot.

##### Plan recovery and revocation

Unique long secrets, controlled resets, protected keys, validity checks and revocation all matter. Biometrics are difficult to replace after compromise, making enrollment and fallback important. Password managers improve unique-secret handling without removing access-control requirements.

##### Worked review check

Why is an unattended authenticated session risky even after an MFA login?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

MFA establishes identity at an event. Session protection, authorization, idle timeouts, endpoint security and revocation still govern subsequent access.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Apply strong local secrets and integrate additional factors through AAA.

**Covered features:** Password policy; MFA; Certificates; Biometrics.

##### Create a strong local recovery identity

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

The local account supplies one knowledge factor. Use an approved AAA/identity service for supported MFA flows; the username command does not add a token or biometric factor.

```text
enable
configure terminal
username recovery privilege 15 algorithm-type scrypt secret <LONG_UNIQUE_RECOVERY_SECRET>
end
```


##### Inspect identity and certificate state

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

Certificate enrollment and MFA integration are platform/identity-service workflows. These commands inspect existing state; they do not assert that MFA is enforced.

```text
show aaa servers
show crypto pki certificates
show ip ssh
show users
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- A password plus PIN is still one factor category.
- Confirm supported certificate authentication and AAA methods for the platform; do not invent an IOS enable MFA command.

##### Command references

- [Cisco C9000 IOS XE resilient infrastructure playbook](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/networking/switches/catalyst-9000-switches/c9000-ios-xe-resilient-infra-pb.html)
- [Catalyst 9300 configuration and command references](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/catalyst-9300-series-switches/series.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
Password + hardware security key → knowledge + possession
Password + PIN → two knowledge secrets, not two factor categories
```


#### Check your understanding

Which pair represents different authentication factors?

- **A.** Password and PIN
- **B.** Password and security key
- **C.** Two passwords
- **D.** Two security questions

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**B. Password and security key**

A password is knowledge; a physical security key is possession.

</details>

Next objective: [5.5 Remote-access and site-to-site IPsec VPNs](#objective-5-5)

<a id="objective-5-5"></a>

### 5.5 — Remote-access and site-to-site IPsec VPNs

**Exam target:** Describe.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.5) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.5/commands)

A VPN creates a protected logical path across an untrusted network. IPsec protects traffic at the IP layer.

#### Build your understanding

- Site-to-site VPNs join networks through gateways. Remote-access VPNs connect individual users or endpoints to an organization.
- IPsec ESP can provide confidentiality, integrity and origin authentication. IKE negotiates security associations and keys. Peers need compatible proposals, identities, traffic selectors and reachable endpoints.
- Tunnel mode encapsulates the original IP packet in a new packet and is common for site-to-site VPNs. A tunnel being up does not prove every application route or access rule is correct.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 2 · Chapters 19](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Separate outer and inner packets

Tunnel mode carries an inner packet inside an outer packet addressed between gateways. ESP protection depends on the negotiated suite. IKE negotiates keys and associations; successful negotiation does not prove that the intended client traffic matches the protection policy.

##### Verify the data path

Check security associations, both-direction counters, routes, selectors, ACLs and MTU. Remote-access protects an endpoint’s organizational access; site-to-site protects network traffic through gateways. An IPsec tunnel is not just any encrypted application session.

##### Worked review check

The tunnel is established but encrypted-packet counters stay zero during a client test. What next?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

Check whether the client route sends traffic to the gateway and whether its addresses match the VPN selectors/policy. Control-plane success does not demonstrate encrypted data forwarding.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Operate an existing IKEv2/IPsec VPN and identify its components.

**Covered features:** Site-to-site; Remote access; IKE/IPsec; Tunnel operation.

##### Inspect security associations and encrypted counters

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** IOS XE router · Catalyst 8000V/8000 lab · feature/license support required

These apply to an existing supported VPN design. Read IKE identity/status, IPsec inbound/outbound packet counters and tunnel routing together. Remote-access VPN configuration depends on the VPN headend product and client.

```text
show crypto ikev2 sa detail
show crypto ipsec sa
show crypto session detail
show interfaces Tunnel10
show ip route
```


##### Recognize route-based IPsec attachment

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** IOS XE VPN-capable router — partial example with prerequisites

This is deliberately a partial attachment example, not a deployable full VPN. LAB-IPSEC must already define compatible strong transforms and IKEv2 identity/keying. The peer requires a matching configuration and return routing.

```text
! Pre-existing IKEv2/IPsec profile LAB-IPSEC and reachable peer required.
enable
configure terminal
interface Tunnel10
 ip address 10.255.0.1 255.255.255.252
 tunnel source GigabitEthernet2
 tunnel destination 198.51.100.2
 tunnel mode ipsec ipv4
 tunnel protection ipsec profile LAB-IPSEC
end
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- A tunnel interface being up is not proof that encrypted application traffic is flowing.
- Check peer reachability, proposal/identity mismatch, routes, selectors/policy, NAT interaction and MTU; use the VPN product’s current deployment guide.

##### Command references

- [Catalyst 8000V router documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/routers/catalyst-8000v-edge-software/series.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
Branch LAN → VPN gateway ═ encrypted Internet tunnel ═ VPN gateway → HQ LAN
Check: negotiation → routes → interesting traffic → security policy → MTU.
```


#### Check your understanding

Which VPN model connects two office networks through gateways?

- **A.** Site-to-site
- **B.** Local console
- **C.** DNS recursion
- **D.** Port security

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**A. Site-to-site**

Site-to-site VPNs protect traffic between networks at different locations.

</details>

Next objective: [5.6 Access control lists](#objective-5-6)

<a id="objective-5-6"></a>

### 5.6 — Access control lists

**Exam target:** Configure and verify.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.6) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.6/commands)

An ACL is an ordered set of match and action rules. The first matching entry wins; unmatched traffic reaches an implicit deny.

#### Build your understanding

- Standard IPv4 ACLs match source IP addresses. Extended ACLs can match protocol, source, destination and ports. A wildcard 0 means “must match”; 1 means “ignore this bit.”
- Apply an ACL to the intended interface and direction. Inbound is checked as traffic enters; outbound as it leaves after route selection. Placement depends on traffic policy; extended ACLs are often near the source.
- Preserve required return and infrastructure traffic. A basic ACL is stateless. Use sequence numbers and show access-lists hit counters to verify behavior; an ACL definition alone does not filter an interface.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 2 · Chapters 6, 7, 8](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Evaluate first-match order

Process entries from top to bottom and stop at the first match. Wildcard zero bits must match; one bits are ignored. A broad permit can shadow a later deny. Standard IPv4 ACLs match sources; extended ACLs add protocol, destination and supported ports.

##### Preserve required return traffic

A stateless ACL does not automatically allow return sessions. DNS may use UDP/TCP; OSPFv2 is IP protocol 89; DHCP has specific client/server behavior. TCP established checks ACK/RST rather than building full firewall state. VTY access-class protects login, not arbitrary transit traffic.

##### Worked review check

Will a TCP 22 deny below a broad permit for the same source subnet block SSH?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

No. The earlier permit already matches. Put the intended specific rule first, then verify attachment, direction and hit counters.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Create, attach and verify IPv4 ACL policies.

**Covered features:** Standard/extended; Wildcards; First match; Implicit deny; Interface/direction.

##### Permit TCP-based HTTPS to a server from a client subnet

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** IOS XE router · Catalyst 8000V/8000 lab · feature/license support required or Layer 3-capable Catalyst switch · IOS XE 26.x · routing license required as applicable

Use Vlan10 on a multilayer switch or the corresponding client-facing routed interface on a router. This policy filters user-to-server-subnet traffic and explicitly permits other IPv4 traffic; it is a separate lab policy from lesson 2.1’s strict allowlist. This permits TCP 443. HTTP/3 over QUIC uses UDP 443 and needs a separate intentional rule.

```text
enable
configure terminal
ip access-list extended USERS-WEB
 10 permit tcp 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.20.20.10 eq 443
 20 deny ip 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255 10.20.20.0 0.0.0.255
 30 permit ip any any
exit
interface Vlan10
 ip access-group USERS-WEB in
end
```


##### Inspect ACL order, attachment and counters

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** Layer 3-capable Catalyst switch · IOS XE 26.x · routing license required as applicable

Generate allowed HTTPS and denied traffic from an actual client behind VLAN 10. A switch-originated ping does not necessarily enter through the filtered SVI.

```text
show ip access-lists USERS-WEB
show ip interface Vlan10
show running-config interface Vlan10
```


##### Detach only this filter when undoing the lab

**Category:** troubleshoot. **Platform/context:** Layer 3-capable Catalyst switch · IOS XE 26.x · routing license required as applicable

Removing an applied filter changes the policy. Detach the correct ACL deliberately, then inspect the interface; leaving an unreferenced ACL definition has no interface-filtering effect.

```text
enable
configure terminal
interface Vlan10
 no ip access-group USERS-WEB in
end
```


##### Separate lab: standard IPv4 ACL for VTY login sources

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** IOS XE router or Catalyst switch; console recovery required; substitute your approved management subnet

**Objective coverage:** 5.6 standard ACL source matching; 4.8 management access

A standard ACL matches only sources. access-class applies it to device logins, separately from the transit interface filter. Validate permitted sources before restricting remote access.

```text
enable
configure terminal
ip access-list standard MGMT-SOURCES
 10 permit 10.99.0.0 0.0.0.255
 20 deny any log
exit
line vty 0 15
 access-class MGMT-SOURCES in
end
show ip access-lists MGMT-SOURCES
show running-config | section line vty
```


**Expected result:** Approved clients in the selected subnet can reach the configured VTY service; other sources are denied. Console access is independent. This does not replace SSH authentication or filter arbitrary transit traffic.

##### Troubleshooting checks

- Basic router ACLs are stateless: return traffic follows its own path and applicable policies.
- SVI router ACLs do not block same-VLAN switched traffic. Use appropriate Layer 2 controls for that different requirement.

##### Command references

- [Catalyst 9300 VLAN configuration guide — IOS XE 26.x](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/switches/lan/catalyst9300/software/release/26-x/configuration_guide/vlan/b_26x_vlan_9300_cg.pdf)
- [Catalyst 9300 configuration and command references](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/catalyst-9300-series-switches/series.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
ip access-list extended USERS
 permit tcp 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.0.2.80 eq 443
 deny ip 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255 any
 permit ip any any
interface g0/0
 ip access-group USERS in
```


#### Check your understanding

What happens if a packet matches no entry in an applied ACL?

- **A.** It is permitted
- **B.** It is implicitly denied
- **C.** It is sent to DNS
- **D.** It restarts the ACL

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**B. It is implicitly denied**

Every ACL ends with an implicit deny for traffic that did not match an explicit entry.

</details>

Next objective: [5.7 Layer 2 security controls](#objective-5-7)

<a id="objective-5-7"></a>

### 5.7 — Layer 2 security controls

**Exam target:** Configure and verify.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.7) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.7/commands)

Access-layer protections defend against local attacks that routed security alone cannot stop.

#### Build your understanding

- Port security limits learned or configured source MAC addresses. Protect drops violating traffic; restrict also records violations; shutdown normally err-disables the port. Sticky learning can add learned addresses to the running configuration.
- DHCP snooping filters DHCP server messages on untrusted ports and builds a binding table. Trust only legitimate server/relay-facing paths. Enable it globally and for the required VLANs.
- Dynamic ARP Inspection checks ARP against trusted bindings or configured ARP ACLs. Incorrect trust settings or missing bindings can break legitimate traffic, including statically addressed hosts.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 2 · Chapters 11, 12](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Keep trust controls separate

DHCP snooping trust permits legitimate server messages on a chosen interface; DAI trust bypasses incoming ARP inspection on its chosen interface. Neither automatically configures the other. Ordinary client ports should not be trusted merely to suppress symptoms.

##### Plan exceptions and recovery

DAI normally uses DHCP snooping bindings; static hosts need an appropriate validated design such as an ARP ACL. Port-security protect/restrict/shutdown have different notification and err-disable outcomes. Sticky entries persist across reboot only when the relevant configuration is saved.

##### Worked review check

After DAI is enabled, static hosts fail but DHCP hosts work. What may be missing?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

A validated IP-to-MAC binding or applicable ARP ACL for the static systems. Diagnose bindings and trust instead of trusting every access port.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Protect access ports and ARP/DHCP at Layer 2.

**Covered features:** Port security; DHCP snooping; Dynamic ARP Inspection.

##### Limit source MAC learning on a host port

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

Sticky entries go into the running configuration; saving is a separate action. Restrict drops violating traffic and records violations. Shutdown is a different violation mode.

```text
enable
configure terminal
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 10
 switchport port-security
 switchport port-security maximum 2
 switchport port-security mac-address sticky
 switchport port-security violation restrict
end
```


##### Build DHCP bindings and inspect ARP

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

Trust only the verified path toward legitimate DHCP/ARP infrastructure. Enable snooping and obtain valid bindings before relying on DAI for DHCP clients. Statically addressed hosts need an appropriate separate ARP-validation design.

```text
enable
configure terminal
ip dhcp snooping
ip dhcp snooping vlan 10
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/24
 ip dhcp snooping trust
 ip arp inspection trust
exit
ip arp inspection vlan 10
end
```


##### Verify bindings, violations and trust state

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

An empty binding table can explain DAI drops for otherwise legitimate DHCP clients. Read trust settings and bindings before disabling inspection.

```text
show port-security interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1
show port-security address
show ip dhcp snooping
show ip dhcp snooping binding
show ip arp inspection
show ip arp inspection statistics
show interfaces status err-disabled
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- Do not mark all client ports trusted to make DHCP work.
- Port-security and wireless/AP/virtualization uplinks can have multiple source MACs; choose limits for the actual role.

##### Command references

- [Catalyst 9300 configuration and command references](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/catalyst-9300-series-switches/series.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
! Global configuration; VLAN 10 and its links already exist.
ip dhcp snooping
ip dhcp snooping vlan 10
ip arp inspection vlan 10
interface g0/24
 ! Trust only the validated server/gateway-facing path.
 ip dhcp snooping trust
 ip arp inspection trust
exit
interface g0/1
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 10
 switchport port-security
 switchport port-security maximum 2
! Plan validated ARP handling for static hosts.
! Verify: show ip dhcp snooping binding; show ip arp inspection
```


#### Check your understanding

Which control helps block rogue DHCP server replies on access ports?

- **A.** DHCP snooping
- **B.** NTP
- **C.** CDP
- **D.** OSPF passive-interface

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**A. DHCP snooping**

DHCP snooping accepts server messages only on trusted paths and filters them on untrusted client ports.

</details>

Next objective: [5.8 Authentication, authorization and accounting](#objective-5-8)

<a id="objective-5-8"></a>

### 5.8 — Authentication, authorization and accounting

**Exam target:** Compare.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.8) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.8/commands)

AAA separates identifying a user, determining permitted actions and recording activity.

#### Build your understanding

- Authentication asks who you are. Authorization determines what you may do. Accounting records what you did and when.
- RADIUS commonly uses UDP 1812 for authentication and 1813 for accounting. TACACS+ commonly uses TCP 49 and separates AAA functions, supporting detailed command authorization.
- A central AAA service provides consistent policy, but its outage behavior matters. Carefully defined local fallback and a tested recovery path prevent management lockout.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 1 · Chapters 6](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-1-9780138229634) · [Volume 2 · Chapters 9](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Follow three functions

Authentication verifies identity, authorization permits actions and accounting records activity. A successful login does not necessarily permit configuration commands. RADIUS commonly uses UDP 1812/1813; TACACS+ uses TCP 49 and separates AAA functions.

##### Distinguish rejection and error

A method list may try a later method after unavailability or an error. An explicit authentication rejection does not normally mean that a local password should bypass it. Test fallback behavior and an authorized recovery path rather than assuming every failure has the same meaning.

##### Worked review check

A reachable AAA server rejects a user. Should local fallback be assumed to override it?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

No. Rejection differs from an unavailable/error condition. Check the method list and documented platform behavior.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Select AAA methods and inspect server state.

**Covered features:** Authentication; Authorization; Accounting; RADIUS/TACACS+.

##### Use a named TACACS+ group and local fallback

**Category:** configure. **Platform/context:** IOS XE device with a securely configured TACACS server object ISE1

Prerequisites: working SSH, a local recovery user and an existing ISE1 server object with address and securely stored shared secret. Configure/test from the console. This is the AAA method-list layer, not a complete AAA server installation.

```text
enable
configure terminal
aaa new-model
aaa group server tacacs+ DEVICE-ADMIN
 server name ISE1
exit
aaa authentication login VTY-LOGIN group DEVICE-ADMIN local
aaa authorization exec VTY-EXEC group DEVICE-ADMIN local
aaa accounting exec VTY-ACCT start-stop group DEVICE-ADMIN
line vty 0 15
 login authentication VTY-LOGIN
 authorization exec VTY-EXEC
 accounting exec VTY-ACCT
 transport input ssh
end
```


##### Inspect servers and sessions

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9300 switch · IOS XE 26.x

Local fallback normally applies when the server is unavailable/errors; a server actively rejecting a user does not necessarily trigger local fallback. Accounting records must be checked on the AAA server too.

```text
show aaa servers
show tacacs
show users
show running-config | section aaa
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- Use current secure shared-secret storage and transport guidance; older key 7 examples are not current best practice.
- RADIUS for access authentication and TACACS+ for device administration are separate designs with different ports and authorization behavior.

##### Command references

- [Cisco C9000 IOS XE resilient infrastructure playbook](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/networking/switches/catalyst-9000-switches/c9000-ios-xe-resilient-infra-pb.html)
- [Catalyst 9300 configuration and command references](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/catalyst-9300-series-switches/series.html)
- [Cisco IOS XE 26 release documentation](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/ios-nx-os-software/ios-xe-26/series.html)

#### Additional concept example

This may use older IOS syntax or an illustrative text diagram. Use the platform-labeled guide above for the intended current lab context.

```text
Login → authenticate identity
Run configure terminal → authorize command
Record login and command → account for activity
```


#### Check your understanding

Which AAA function determines whether a user may execute a command?

- **A.** Authentication
- **B.** Authorization
- **C.** Accounting
- **D.** Address resolution

<details>
<summary>Answer and explanation</summary>

**B. Authorization**

Authorization controls allowed actions after identity has been established.

</details>

Next objective: [5.9 WPA, WPA2 and WPA3 security](#objective-5-9)

<a id="objective-5-9"></a>

### 5.9 — WPA, WPA2 and WPA3 security

**Exam target:** Describe.

[Open objective](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.9) · [Open command guide](https://ianlin-smci.github.io/ccna-study-lab/#/lesson/5.9/commands)

Wireless authentication and encryption evolved to address weaknesses in older protocols.

#### Build your understanding

- WPA introduced TKIP as a transitional improvement over WEP. WPA2 commonly uses AES-CCMP; legacy TKIP configurations should not be treated as equivalent to modern AES security.
- WPA3-Personal uses SAE for password-authenticated key establishment and improves resistance to offline password guessing. WPA3 also requires protected management frames.
- Personal modes use a shared password; Enterprise uses 802.1X/EAP and an authentication server. A strong PSK is still necessary; transition modes and client compatibility affect the protection actually negotiated.

#### Supporting reading — Official Cert Guide, Second Edition

Suggested reading: [Volume 2 · Chapters 3](https://www.ciscopress.com/store/ccna-200-301-official-cert-guide-volume-2-9780138214951)

##### Keep mechanisms distinct

Enterprise authentication uses 802.1X/EAP and a server; EAP-TLS uses certificates. Personal security uses shared-credential mechanisms such as WPA2 PSK or WPA3 SAE. AES-CCMP protects data but does not alone identify the authentication method.

##### Read negotiated protection

WEP and TKIP have legacy weaknesses. Hiding an SSID is not encryption. WPA3 includes protected management-frame requirements; transition mode and client capability influence the actual result. Verify the client’s negotiation as well as configured policy.

##### Worked review check

Does disabling SSID broadcast replace WPA2/WPA3 security?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

No. Wireless exchanges can reveal the network name. Apply the intended authentication and encryption policy regardless of SSID visibility.

</details>

#### Platform-labeled command guide

Inspect negotiated wireless security and compare current alternatives.

**Covered features:** WPA/TKIP; WPA2/AES; WPA3/SAE; Personal/Enterprise.

##### Read the WLAN and a client’s negotiated security

**Category:** verify. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9800 wireless controller · IOS XE · not AireOS or a switch CLI

Read AKM, cipher and protected-management-frame settings, and compare with the connected client. An advertised transition mode can result in clients negotiating different security.

```text
show wlan name STAFF
show wlan summary
show wireless client mac-address aaaa.bbbb.cccc detail
```


##### Recognize the WPA3-Personal building blocks

**Category:** reference. **Platform/context:** Catalyst 9800 wireless controller · IOS XE · not AireOS or a switch CLI — reference, not a complete WLAN

These identify WPA3, SAE and required PMF. A full WPA3 profile also needs the correct supported password/cipher settings and policy mapping for that release. Lesson 5.10 provides the complete WPA2 exam-focused lab.

```text
! WLAN configuration context; inspect security wpa ? on your release.
! security wpa wpa3
! security wpa akm sae
! security pmf mandatory
```


##### Troubleshooting checks

- Do not configure WEP/TKIP on a current deployment to reproduce an old security comparison.
- Enterprise security needs 802.1X/EAP and a configured authentication service, not a shared-PSK-only WLAN.

##### Command references

- [Catalyst 9800 controller configuration guides](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/wireless/catalyst-9800-series-wireless-controllers/series.html)
